Commentary.Commentary: We are back again. England's players stride out to the middle. The two left-handers, Kusal Perera and Lahiru Thirimanne, are out in the middle as well. James Anderson, who had a 6-fer in the first innings, will start with the ball for England. 'Play' is the call and we get underway again. 2 slips and a gully in place.

Right then, time for Lanka to strap the boots on again, that is to build on this lead of 37 that they have. With their skipper saying that he expects 240-250 to be competitive, it will be interesting to see how the batters go about. They have a bit of time and will look to play watchfully, before upping the ante. Can England though start cashing in on the growing slowness of the track? Let's find out as the players step out shortly...

It was a decent bowling performance from Lanka but they would be kicking themselves for allowing crucial partnerships at various stages to chip away at the deficit. It was the spinners show, or should we say the Embuldeniya show? The left-arm orthodox bowler was the pick of the bowlers, bagging 7, with Mendis and Perera snaring 1 each. Oshada displayed brilliant presence of mind, at short leg, in running Root out on the last over of Day 3.

Batting in response to the Lankans' first innings total of 381, the England batters got off to the worst imaginable start - losing both their openers cheaply again. However, Bairstow and Root, who had been in familiar waters in the last game, resurrected their team to safety. Root, along with Buttler and Bess, helped England get close to Sri Lanka's total, before he himself fell, for a magnificent 186. And England fell short of the Lankan total by 37 runs in the end.

So, Chandimal, before the start of the match, said that he was looking at a lead of 40 runs that they could build on. And they have got somewhere around that. But then, the divide was largely bridged by Joe Root's fantastic 186. If not for that, England would have found themselves in a more precipitous situation.

Review time! It is for an LBW against Leach, who is given out, on-field. Looks plumb, unless there was some bat. England would have also felt that we have a review, might as well use it. Anyway, let's see what technology has to say...

OUT! LBW! That was plumb, to the naked eye. Umpire Dharmasena, raises his finger for the second time, after the third umpire conveyed his decision after the review was taken. Leach gets to the other end and then flashes the 'T'. No bat on the ball there and Ball Tracker gives Leach the marching orders. ENGLAND BOWLED OUT FOR 344!
FOUR! Oh, yes!!! Runs for Jimmy. He makes his intentions clear. Reverse sweeps a full ball from the rough outside off and nails it down to third man for a boundary. The deficit is now 37 runs.
England are away on Day 4! Leach once again goes on the back foot and works it with the spin to fine leg for a run.
Flatter and on off, Leach goes on the back foot and defends it down on the leg side.
Presses forward to a full ball and drives it towards deepish mid off, not taking the run.
Fuller and on off, Leach hits it across the line, with the spin, but finds the mid on fielder.
Full and floated on middle, Leach gets behind the line and pushes it back to the bowler.
Lasith Embuldeniya to operate from the other end. Can he make it 8?

Back to fuller length, on the off pole, defended to the off side.
This time it is flatter and around off, he rocks back and pushes it back to the bowler.

Right, we are set to get underway on Day 4 then! Jack Leach and James Anderson walk out to the middle. The Sri Lankan players have taken their positions on the field. Dilruwan Perera to finish off his pending over. Can he finish the innings in his remaining 4 balls? Let's find out...

Dinesh Chandimal says that it was a tough day for them with this heat. Shares that normally they don't get so much heat in Galle. Credits all the bowlers for putting in the efforts and also the fielders for showing a lot of energy. Smiles and says that they always discuss how to get Root out who is batting at a different level and credits him for his knock. Feels that if they get him out quickly in the next innings, that will be crucial for them. Mentions that if they get the last wicket quickly, it will be great. And then, with a lead of 40 or so, he hopes to get 200 runs on board. Overall, DC feels that 240-250 might be good on this track.

Pitch report - Russel Arnold provides the update on the pitch. On the weather, he says it is nice - blue skies. Coming to the pitch, there is a lot of dust and Russel reckons that it is pretty dry. Plenty of areas for the bowlers to bowl to, he adds. In line with the stumps, Arnold says that Embuldeniya gained a lot of turn from there. He feels Sri Lanka might have a fairly challenging time, batting second. We are in for an interesting day. All to play for!

The Englishmen now trail by just 42 runs but have only 1 wicket in hand. Unlike England, whose seamers got all the wickets, for the Lankans, Lasith got 7 and Ramesh snared 1. Now, they would look to clean up the last wicket quickly and probably bat for 2 sessions before having a final crack against the England batsmen. Stay tuned for what promises to be a gripping day ahead...

England had begun Day 3 at 98/2. Bairstow and Root could only add 18 runs to the overnight total before the former fell. However, Root stitched valuable partnerships with Buttler and Bess and brought England to the cusp of Sri Lanka's total. However, he fell, unfortunately, in the last over, 14 runs shy of what could have been another epic double ton.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of Day 4 between these two sides. The match is epicly poised and with Sri Lanka gunning for a victory, and the pitch slowing down, a result might well be on the cards. So, what happened on Day 3 and what to look forward now?
... Day 4, Session 1...

Lanka will be happy with any kind of lead they get as any kind of lead could prove very vital. The wicket seemed to have worsened more in the last session and that is not a good sign for England as they have to bat last. Another important day awaits. Do join us for Day 4 at 1000 local (0430 GMT). Until then, cheers!

They managed to take England pretty close to Sri Lanka's total. At one stage, it seemed like they would take the lead, but wickets right at the end of the day has turned the tide into Sri Lanka's favor by just. Their bowling was all about Lasith Embuldeniya. He has 7 off the 9 wickets that fell and he will be eyeing the 8th on Day 4 as quickly as possible.

Another masterclass from Joe Root! Had it not been for him, England might have been well behind in this game. They were reeling at 132-4 with Root holding one end up and wickets falling at the other. However, Buttler first and Bess then showed grit and grinded it out there with their skipper. Jos and Root added almost a 100-run stand. Bess and Root then put up another top class stand.

So wickets right at the end probably means that it is Sri Lanka who will be heading into Day 4 as the happier of the two sides. However, they are probably ahead by just a bit in this game. For England, they have just the one man to thank for the position they are in right now and that is their skipper.

And now, the third umpire comes into play. Replays roll in and it is seen that Root is well short. A very good innings from the skipper comes to an end. With that big wicket, IT IS STUMPS ON DAY 3!

The Islanders will come out and will want to bundle the tail rather quickly and would not want to see the tail wag. England would look at Root and would hope that he can reduct the deficit. An interesting final session of play awaits. Join us in a short while for the third and final session of Day 3.

Root and Buttler started off in their typical fashion. They dispatched the loose deliveries and respected the good ones. They also stitched their 50-run stand and Buttler reached his half-century too. It was then that the debutant Ramesh Mendis, struck and broke this promising stand. Curran came out then and he looked solid right until the stroke of Tea, where he ended up losing his wicket cheaply. Embuldeniya also got a 5-fer and would look to scalp a few more wickets.
An even session based on the way things have panned out, you would say. The first hour of this session would belong to England and the second hour should be Sri Lanka's.

OUT! CAUGHT! Sri Lanka have struck right at the stroke of Tea, which is a very nice time to scalp a wicket. Lasith gets his 5th wicket of the game and he will be very happy with his show so far. Floats it up nicely and around off, Curran lunges forward and looks to block this one out but the ball spins away and kisses the outside edge. Goes towards Thirimanne at first slip and he is not going to make a meal of this. Takes it easily and the new ball has done the trick for the Islanders. With that, IT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 3!

We are back for the second session of play on Day 3. The batters for England, Joe Root and Jos Buttler make their way out into the middle. Lasith Embuldeniya to begin with the ball. Let's go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

The session though began brilliantly for Sri Lanka! They got two in the first hour itself but as the ball got old, the bowlers seemed less effective. Batting got easier as there was no zip off the surface and the turn was also slow. To add to that, only Lasith Embuldeniya has been the one picking wickets and they need the others to supprt him. The hosts would know another wicket and they would be into the bowling all-rounders. An interesting second session awaits. Will the fightback continue or will Sri Lanka rule the roost? Join us at around 1240 local (0710 GMT) for the second session.

A good fightback then from England after Drinks! They have not lost a wicket and have almost avoided the follow-on. Once again it is their skipper Root who is the mainstay and now Buttler has given him very good support. However, they would know the job is not done as of now and they need to keep batting.

We are all set to begin! The Sri Lankan players stride out to the middle, followed by Jonny Bairstow and Joe Root. Dilruwan Perera will start with the ball.

Joe Root is up for a chat. He says that Day 3 is an important day and they worked really hard on the field in hot and humid conditions. Goes onto say that he just felt good and rolled with it. Adds that the conditions changed pretty quickly. Goes onto say that he tried to change the bowlers lengths and tried to dictate terms. Goes onto say that they are talking all the time and good thing for him is that he looks to defend off the front foot and everybody has got to bat their own way. Tells that they are trying to make sure and commit to whatever plan they have got.

Pitch report -  Russel Arnold says that the pitch is changing a bit but it is still very good for batting. Tells that there is variable turn and bounce on this pitch and the Sri Lankan bowlers will have to rely on that. Adds that there is rough appearing on the wicket and they will have to target that rough. Says that Dilruwan Perera has to try and get the straighter one to come back in. Adds that the spinners have to be patient.

England in their reply had a poor start. They lost their openers in quick succession thanks to some lovely bowling from Embuldeniya but Root once again looked at his best and he is in a solid partnership with Jonny Bairstow. They still trail by 283 runs and their first target will be to wipe off the deficit. Join us in a while.

Sri Lanka started Day 2 on top but they lost 2 wickets in quick succession but contributions from Niroshan Dickwella and Dilruwan Perera was took them to 381 which is a decent score on this wicket. Anderson was the star with the ball as he picked up a 6-fer with Wood picking up 3.
We have had two interesting days of Test cricket and Day 3 promises to be another cracker of a Test match. It is nicely poised at the moment. Who will move ahead on Day 3?
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Right, so when England step out to bat again on Day 3, they would want this partnership to continue for some more, unless they feel they have gained some parity. As far as the Sri Lankans are concerned though, they would look to snare a few quick wickets in the first session on Day 3. In whose way will the first session swing? Join us on Sunday, 24th January 2021, at 1000 AM Local (0430 AM GMT), to find out. Until then, take care and cheers...

Niroshan Dickwella is caught up for a chat. He says that he talked to the batting coach and the support staff regarding his batting. Mentions that he though is disappointed to not make a century. Further says that they lost a couple of wickets early and then a few partnerships were stitched. He though mentions that the wicket was a bit two-paced, as compared to the last game. Niroshan Dickwella says that there is enough for the bowlers and the odd ball is turning too, so they would look to come out tomorrow and look to take wickets.

All the 10 wickets fell to the seamers, for England, with Anderson being the standout performer. James Anderson got 6 wickets to his name, with Wood getting 3 and Curran getting the last wicket of Perera. Stepping out to bat in response, England got off to a disastrous start as they lost both their openers cheaply. But then, Jonny and Joe got together and stitched an important unbeaten stand of 93 to put the Englishmen back on track. Root is strong at 67 from just 77 balls while Bairstow played second fiddle to his skipper.

Day 2 started off with Angelo Mathews falling early, soon to be followed by Ramesh Mendis, the debutant as well. After that Dickwella stitched a very good partnership with Perera, before the former fell short of his maiden hundred in whites. But Dilruwan Perera continued strong and along with a good couple of stands in the end, managed to take the Sri Lankan total to a strong 381.

What a terrific day of Test match cricket it has been. England are 98/2 and would feel that they are fighting, as we also draw the conclusion that Sri Lanka would be happy with the way they are, in the match right now. The match is still tantalisingly poised though.
Another one on off, pushed back down the ground off the front foot. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2!
On off, kept out off the front foot.
Fuller and darted on leg, Bairstow looks to flick it to the leg side but is beaten to get rapped on the pads. There is an appeal from the bowler but the umpire does not give it.
Tossed up on off, defended off the front foot towards the off side.
Darted on leg, Jonny pushes it to the on side.
Fuller and around off, Jonny blocks it out to the off side.
Just the one from the over. 98/2. Full length delivery around off, Joe strides forward and keeps that one out.
Flatter and around off, Bairstow rocks back and clips it in front of square on the on side. Takes a single.
Flat and around off, Jonny keeps it out on the leg side.
Floated around off, pushed back to Dilruwan.
On middle, clipped to the man at short fine leg.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Bairstow gets a long way across and manages to sweep it to the right of the man at 45. The fielder gets there and stops it.
On off, kept out off the front foot by Root. Runs coming thick and fast as England closing in on 100 runs.
Flatter and outside off, Root helps it past the slips and towards third man for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Flatter and outside off, Root goes on the back foot and cuts it powerfully through point for another boundary.
FOUR! Now that's brilliant! Absolute world class! Full and outside off, Root brings out the reverse sweep as he gets it past point. The ball races to the fence for a boundary.
Fuller and on leg, pushed from within the crease towards the leg side.
FOUR! Another sweep and Root fetches a boundary! Full and down leg, Root once again brings out the broom and nails it through to square leg for a boundary.
Full and on off, clipped to the man at short mid-wicket.

NOT OUT! The original decision stays. Fullish length delivery on middle and leg, Bairstow goes a long way across and looks to flick it on the leg side. To the naked eye, he seems to have missed and the ball hits his pads. There is a huge appeal from the Lankans for a lbw but the umpire is unmoved there. Dinesh Chandimal has a chat with his teammates and flashes the 'T', rather hesitatingly. So, there is no bat involved as the ball passes it.

Review taken! Sri Lanka have taken yet another review against Jonny Bairstow.Let's see what the replays show. Ultra Edge comes on and there is no bat involved. Now the Ball Tracker comes on and it shows to be Umpire's Call on hitting the wickets. Bairstow survives.
On off, worked to square leg for a single.
Around off, Jonny taps it to the man at short mid-wicket. The fielder there misfields and ends up conceding a single.
Full length ball around off, Root sweeps it to square leg for a single.

A mild appeal for lbw but not given. Full length delivery on middle, Root looks to sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads. An appeal but it is not given. Chandimal has a word with the keeper but decides against taking the review. Hmm... so there must have been some bat or glove there.
Flatter on off, JB punches it off the back foot this time to the off side.
Tossed up on off, pushed down to mid on this time by Jonny.
Tossed up outside off, Jonny makes a leave this time, a watchful one.
Fuller on middle, swept by Root for a single to square leg.
On off, kept out towards the side of the pitch on the leg side.
A full toss to start a new spell as Root helps it towards deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs. Root gets to yet another 50 in Tests as he shows how to bat on spinning tracks.
Lasith Embuldeniya is back on. 8-3-16-2 from him so far.
That is Joe Root's first run in that area. Around off, JR hits it down to long on and takes a single.
FOUR! Too easy for Root. Full toss, around off, JR lunges down and paddles it nicely behind square on the off side, for a boundary.
Floated delivery, Root keeps it out behind square on the leg side.
Outside off, dabbed to the off side.
Sweeps it to deep square leg for two runs.

An appeal for LBW but not given. Was it missing the leg pole? That was why umpire Kumar was not interested. Flatter ball on middle and leg, it pitches and goes towards the leg pole line. Root gets a long way across and looks to work it on the leg side but misses and gets hit on the pads. There is an appeal but nothing from the umpire.
Short of good length and around off, Bairstow punches it off the back foot towards cover-point.
A bumper outside off, trying to surprise Bairstow there but Jonny does well to sway away from the line of the ball there.
Another back of a length ball around off, Bairstow punches it off the back foot towards the leg side.
Short of good length and around off, Jonny punches it off the back foot this time to covers.
Good length and around off, clipped towards mid-wicket by Root for a single.
Length and around off, Root plays it off the back foot towards the off side.
Looped up delivery on off, Jonny strides forward in defence there.
Loopy and around off, pushed back to Dilruwan Perera.
Flatter delivery, Jonny Bairstow keeps it out on the on side.

Lands it on middle, it pitches and spins away, down the leg side. Bairstow moves well across. Initially he looked to play at it but then lets it be. The keeper fails to collect it and the ball goes down to the long stop region. A couple, off byes.
On the shorter side and outside off, Jonny rocks back and fends it out.
FOUR! Very safe shot. Good option. Loopy ball around off, Jonny skips out of his track and lofts it well over the bowler's head and wide of the man at mid on as well.
Length and on off, kept out off the back foot by Root this time.

Length and around middle and leg, Root looks to tuck it to the leg side but misses it as he gets rapped on the pads. There is a desperate appeal from the bowler but just a shake of head from the umpire. Maybe missing leg is what the umpire must have thought.
A nice combo of front foot and back foot strokes on display by Root as he keeps this one out towards the off side off the back foot.
And again pushes this fuller length ball down the ground towards mid on off the back foot does Root.
Now comes on the front foot as he blocks this fuller length ball around off to the off side.
Length and around off, Root blocks it right from within the crease as he welcomes Fernando for a new spell.
Asitha Fernando is back on. 3-1-11-0 from him so far.
Outside off, kept out on the off side.
Sweeps this to deep backward square leg for a run.

NOT OUT! A wayward ball to take a review. One of the worst ever reviews taken, in a long time. Flatter delivery around off, Joe Root comes across and forward and offers no stroke there. He ends up getting hit on the pads. There is a huge appeal for a LBW but the umpire shakes his head. Dinesh has a chat with his players and takes the review in the end. It is sent upstairs. There was no bat at all and hence we go to Ball Tracker. Pitching - Outside off. Impact - Outside off. Wickets - Missing by many a mile.

Sri Lanka take the review against Root. Let's see what the replays have to show. No stroke offered reckons the third umpire so we move to Ball Tracker directly. Here comes the Ball Tracker, Pitching outside off, Impact is outside off and wickets missing. So the Lankans too lose a review.
Both batters have swept well. Loopy delivery around the off pole, Jonny sweeps it to the man at deep square leg for a run.
Floated around off, Root gets down and sweeps it through backward square leg. Takes one.
Fullish length delivery around the off stump, Joe covers his stumps and blocks it out.
Flatter and on middle, pulled towards square leg off the back foot for a single.

FOUR! Innovation from Root and he is all over the debutant. Bowls a tossed up ball on off and middle, Root goes for the reverse sweep and gets it through the backward point region and into the fence. 3rd boundary off the over.
Floated on leg, tucked towards the leg side.
FOUR! Runs flowing here! 50-run stand is also up! Tossed up down leg, Root sweeps it towards fine leg and gets a boundary.
Tossed up around off, Root gets a thin edge as the ball goes past the short leg fielder.
FOUR! Root is putting the debutant under pressure there. Tossed up ball down leg, Root gets down on one knee and sweeps it behind square on the leg side and gets a boundary. 50 up for England also.
Keeps the fuller length delivery out on the on side.
On the shorter side around the off stump, Jonny Bairstow clips it to the leg side.
FOUR! Swept away and swept for four. Floated ball on the off pole line, Jonny Bairstow gets down on one knee and sweeps it well wide of the man at short fine leg for a boundary.
Floated delivery outside the off pole, Bairstow taps it back to Perera.
Flat and outside off, Jonny gets across again and manages to fend this one off.
Full and outside off, Jonny gets across and looks to drive but he misses it. Beauty. Perera got it off the rough.
FOUR! Swept nicely! Tossed up on leg, Root gets down to play the sweep and nails it right in the gap at square leg as Angelo Mathews in the deep gives up the chase.
Slightly fuller on middle, Root turns it to the leg side off the back foot this time.
Flatter and around middle, Jonny tucks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Floated on leg, clipped to short leg.
Floated and going down leg, Bairstow does not play at it.
Tossed up on middle, clipped towards mid-wicket for a single by Root.
Ramesh Mendis comes onto bowl in his debut Test.
Flat and outside off, Jonny goes back and fends it out on the off side.
BEATEN! This is a good start for Dilruwan. Bowls it fuller and outside off, JB looks to defend that but misses there.
Around off, Jonny Bairstow plays that out.

Pitching outside the line of off stump. It is a flatter delivery, pitches outside off and comes back in. Jonny Bairstow goes back but does not offer a shot there. No chance for a LBW as it pitched outside off.
Full and outside the off stump, Bairstow comes forward and looks to drive but ends up getting an inside edge onto his pads there.
Flat and well outside off, Jonny rocks back and looks to but but he misses to do so.

DRINKS! A good passage of play for any Test cricket fan. The Sri Lankan bowlers started beautifully with Lakmal and Embuldeniya keeping it tight. The latter though managed to scalp both the English openers cheaply. Since then it is Root and Bairstow who once again like the previous Test are fighting it out to establish a platform for their side. Still they are to play 21 overs in the session. How long can these two go? We will get to know after this short break. A change in bowling though as Dilruwan Perera comes into the attack now.
Outside off, Joe Root watchfully leaves that alone.
Flat ball on middle and off, Joe Root goes back and plays it very late, to the leg side.
Full length ball on off, defended back to the bowler.
Flat delivery on top of leg, Root rocks back and keeps it out on the leg side.
Full length delivery on off and middle, Jonny gets down and sweeps it down to deep backward square leg. Takes one. Lasith is not worried about the batsmen getting down to sweep him.
Very full and on the pads, Joe glances it through square leg for a single.
Length and around off, clipped towards fine leg for a single by Root.
Low full toss outside off, Root punches it to short cover. He smiles knowing that it was gift and he missed out a boundary there.
Length and around off, punched off the back foot by Jonny towards mid on for a single.
Fuller and on middle, Root clips it towards deep mid-wicket and gets a single to his name.
Length and outside off, Root shoulders arms to it.

FOUR! Nicely done! Fernando bowls one on the pads, Root just about comes inside the line and gets some wood on the ball as it goes past the diving keeper and into the fine leg fence this time for another boundary.
On off, Root swings it to deep square leg and takes a run.
Stabs this on the off side for a dot.
On off and middle, Joe keeps it out to the man at leg slip.
Drifts it on middle, Joe Root rocks back and plays it behind square on the off side. Takes two as third man cuts it off.
Full length delivery around the off pole, Root keeps it out.
Very full length ball on middle, Joe Root flicks it on the leg side.
Fuller and around off, Jonny plays a free flowing drive but fails to pierce the gap at covers.
FOUR! Punched! Short of good length and around off, Bairstow covers the swing on this one as he punches it past point and the ball goes into the fence at deep point for a boundary.
Length and outside off, Jonny does not bother to play at it though.
Length and around off, watchfully kept out by Bairstow this time.
BEATEN! Some swing there! Length and in that channel around off, Bairstow is drawn on the front foot push but the ball just about shapes away, beating the outside edge of Bairstow's bat.
Fuller in length and around off, Jonny plays it down the track towards the bowler.
Root is good off the front foot and the back foot. Flat delivery, outside off, Joe Root camps back and pushes it to the man at point.
This time he connects on the paddle sweep. It goes to the right of fine leg and they take a couple.
In the channel outside off, Joe leaves it alone.
Gets down to paddle this full delivery but misses and gets hit on the body.

Leading edge... oh... Jonny should thank his stars there. Very full length delivery on middle and leg, Bairstow looks to turn it to the vacant mid-wicket region but ends up getting a leading edge. It is uppish, and to his luck, goes wide of the bowler, on the off side. They take one.
Full and just outside off, JB prods forward and blocks it out. The Sri Lankan players are encouraging LE here.
Short of good length around middle and leg, Root plays it off the back foot towards mid on. A good first over for Asitha Fernando too.
Length and outside off, Root has no problems in leaving this one.
Length and on leg, Root clips it off the back foot towards square leg now.
Nice shape there for Fernando too! Length and swinging away outside off, Root lets it be as the ball moves further away from his reach after pitching.
On off, Joe defends it solidly towards the off side off the back foot once again.
Length ball in off, Root goes deep inside his crease and tucks it to the leg side this time.
Asitha Fernando is into the attack now.

Bairstow wants a single but his skipper sends him back here. Fuller and on the middle pole, Jonny Bairstow taps it to the square leg region. He looks for a single and comes down but Root sends him back.
Outside off, Jonny lets that be.
Flat delivery around the off stump line, the English skipper camps on the back foot and clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! 'It's okay' says Dickwella to Lasith. Floated outside the off stump, Joe gets down and slog sweeps it through mid-wicket.
This one is flatter and around the off pole line, the England Test captain goes back and fends it out.
Floated ball outside the off pole line, the English captain rocks back and taps it on the off side.
FOUR! Clipped away! Lakmal strays one on the pads of Bairstow who waits for the ball to come before flicking it through square leg. The ball races to the fence there.
Fuller and around off, Bairstow keeps it out off the back foot once again.
Good length and around off, Bairstow is on the back foot and he plays it to the off side.
Length ball on middle, Root clips it through mid-wicket and crosses ends with Bairstow. A single added to the total.
Slightly shorter in length, Root hops inside his crease and then defends it.
Good length and around off, Root goes right behind in his crease and then blocks it out with a straight bat.
Just a touch short, outside the off pole, JR camps back and tucks it to mid-wicket. Takes a run.
Fuller in length and on off and middle, Joe Root fends it out to the off side.
Flatter and on top of middle, Jonny goes back and clips it in front of square on the on side. Takes one.
Fuller in length ball outside off, Root looks to defend but ends up getting it off the outer half. It goes through the carpet, wide of the man at second slip, to the third man region. A single taken.
Flatter and outside off, Joe rocks back and cuts but point runs to his right and stops that.
Once again the openers fail to give England a start. Now the onus falls on Joe Root to bail England out from this troubled waters as he comes out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! Ohh... that's off the edge. And it has been taken as well. Both the England openers are gone. Full and on middle, it pitches and moves away. Zak is made to play at that. He comes forward and looks to defend it. But he ends up getting an outside edge there. It goes straight into the hands of Lahiru Thirimanne at first slip, who takes it.
Length and outside offf, Bairstow makes a leave to see off the over. Sri Lanka keeping it tight.
Another short one on middle, Crawley pulls it once again but this time there is protection out there, in the deep, on the leg side, and just a single results.
Fuller and around off, Crawley comes slightly on the front foot to push it to the leg side.
Length and well outside off, Crawley does not offer a shot to it.
Another length ball around off, Crawley is comfortable to dab it off the back foot towards point.
Length and around off, Crawley blocks it off the back foot.

Edged.... but drops short. Floated ball outside off, Jonny Bairstow comes forward in defence but ends up getting an outside edge there. Luckily though, it falls short of the man at slip. An excellent over for Embuldeniya comes to an end.
BEATEN! The Sri Lankan wicket-keeper was very excited there. Lasith lands it full and around off, it pitches and moves away. Beats the outside edge of Bairstow as he came forward to defend that.
Full and outside off, Bairstow taps it to the off side.
Full length ball on off and middle, Jonny defends it back on the track.
Jonny Bairstow once again comes out early to bat at number 3.

Review time! Sibley has been given out LBW by the on-field umpire but he challenges it. Lets see what the replays show. The Ultra Edge comes on and there is a flat line on it when the ball passes the bat. Now comes the Ball Tracker and it shows Three Reds. England lose a wicket as well as a review.

OUT! It is a good decision. Full length delivery on middle and leg, Dom looks to flick that but to the naked eye, he seems to have missed it. Gets rapped on the pads and there is an appeal for a LBW. The umpire thinks and thinks before finally raising the finger. Sibley has a chat with Zak, about whether to take the review or not. The dilly-dallyness of the umpire makes him flash the 'T'. It goes upstairs. There is no bat involved, as per UltraEdge. Ball Tracker is in.... THREE REDS! Another failure for Dom Sibley. Sri Lanka and Lasith Embuldeniya though, are off to a great start.
Ohh goodness! Embuldeniya bowls it full and outside off, it pitches and breaks away, Sibley goes back but then lets it be. Sharp turn there.
Length and outside off, Zak has nothing doing as he leaves it alone.
Length and outside off, left alone by Crawley this time.
FOUR! England and Crawley are underway! Short and outside off, Crawley hangs on the back foot and then pulls it powerfully through mid-wicket and fetches a boundary.
Another length ball but a bit closer to off, Crawley is aware of his sticks as he shoulders arms to this one.
Length and outside off, Crawley watches the ball and then decides not to play at it.
Length and around off, Crawley taps it to point now.
Another maiden. The English are 0/0. Full length delivery outside off, Dom prods forward and dabs it on the off side.
In the channel outside the off pole line, Sibley pushes it to the off side.
This time Lasith drags the length back and bowls it flatter, outside the off pole, tapped to the off side.
Fuller in length delivery outside the off pole, Dom defends it to the off side.
Outside off, nudged to the off side.
Little bit of turn this time. Lands it full and outside off, it breaks away after pitching. DS leaves it alone.

Lakmal bowls it from wide of the crease and gets it to angle into off from a length. The ball though does not come in as Suranga expected and Crawley makes a leave. 3 maidens to start for Sri Lanka with the ball.
Length and outside off, it straightens after pitching as Crawley drags his bat back inisde the line of the ball.
Length and outside off, not in the hitting zone of Crawley as he makes a leave.
Length delivery on off, Zak stays on the backfoot and defends it down to the bowler.
An inswinger from Lakmal now but it starts outside off. Crawley does well to leave this one.
BEATEN! Some shape for Lakmal. Length ball away from off, Crawley looks to swat it through the off side but misses it as the ball goes past his outside edge.
End of the over. Back-to-back maidens. Flatter ball, outside the off stump line, Dom Sibley dabs it on the off side.
Floated delivery, outside the off stump. Sibley lets that one be.
Full length delivery, blocked to the off side.
Full length delivery, outside the off pole line, left alone.
Full and outside the off pole, Sibley comes forward but ends up leaving it.
Starts off with a flatter delivery outside off, Dom reaches out and taps it to the covers region.
Who will partner Lakmal from the other end? It will spin to partner the pacer. Lasith Embuldeniya comes to bowl from the other end.
Comfortably behind that one. A maiden to start. Full length ball on the middle pole, Crawley gets behind the line and blocks it out.
Again, just a little bit of shape. Lakmal lands it full and outside off, it pitches and goes away, Zak watchfully leaves it alone.
Inward movement there. Lands it full and outside off, it pitches and comes back in. ZC though, is aware of his off pole, and shoulders arms to let that through. Very close to the off stump that.
Good start from Suranga. Full length delivery on middle, Zak Crawley defends it to the leg side.
Again, a bit of shape away. This one is on a length and well outside off, it pitches and bounces sharply. Crawley lets that one be too. Good carry through to the keeper there.
A little bit of shape away rightaway. Full length delivery outside off, shaping away just a touch. Zak lets it be.
